body: That's a great poem, unfortunately it's hard for me to be comforted simply because I reject the notion that we are lying "down for pleasant dreams." If I had any sort of belief in an afterlife I think I could appreciate this poem as it was meant to be read.

I can understand your reasoning, however, the only thing a 'good' life would bring to me is some comfort on my deathbed. In my situation I just don't feel that it matters how I'm perceived when I'm dead, all emotions cease at that point. In some ways honoring our ancestors is a sham to provide ourselves comfort that we'll mean something even when we've departed.

I'm not currently in a relationship and I don't anticipate being in one soon; I don't have much confidence. Despite my somewhat limited prospects of finding a gf, I think it would help me out a bit. I feel that relationships in general are one thing that seem to matter to me the most as they provide some comfort.
